w: Eero Saarinen designed this 630-foot catenary arch in 1947, though construction didn't start until 1963 and finished in 1965 at a cost of $13 million. Stainless steel and weighted to balance perfectly, it's the world's tallest arch, standing on the exact 1764 site where St Louis was founded.
s: World's tallest arch marks the city's 1764 founding spot
_facts: designed by Eero Saarinen in 1947, a 630-foot stainless steel weighted catenary arch
construction ran 1963-1965 at a cost of $13 million
the world's tallest arch, standing on the 1764 founding site of St Louis

w: Founder Henry Shaw's namesake garden holds a herbarium of more than 7.5 million specimens, the second largest in North America after the New York Botanical Garden. Its Peter H. Raven Library covers 85 percent of everything published on plant taxonomy and systematic botany.
s: Shaw's Garden: 7.5 million specimens, one code, MO
_facts: founded by philanthropist Henry Shaw, informally known as Shaw's Garden
herbarium holds over 7.5 million specimens, second largest in North America
Peter H. Raven Library holds 85% of all literature published on systematic botany

w: James Eads began this Mississippi crossing in 1867, finished it in 1874 -- the first bridge south of the Missouri River and, since none of the earlier ones survived, the oldest bridge on the river today. Foundations reached over 100 feet below water using then-record pneumatic caissons.
s: 1874 bridge with the deepest caissons yet attempted
_facts: designed by James Buchanan Eads, built 1867-1874
first bridge across the Mississippi south of the Missouri River, and the oldest surviving bridge on the river
foundations over 100 feet below water using then-record pneumatic caissons
520-foot center arch, the longest rigid span built at the time, and pioneered large-scale structural steel

w: Opened in 1876, this 1,326-acre park hosted the 1904 World's Fair and that year's Summer Olympics on the same ground. Bounded by Washington University and Kingshighway, it holds the zoo, art museum, history museum and the Muny, and a $100 million restoration has revived prairie and wetland habitat.
s: 1904 World's Fair and Olympics, same acreage
_facts: opened 1876, covers 1,326 acres in western St Louis
hosted the 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition and the 1904 Summer Olympics
home to the St Louis Zoo, Art Museum, Missouri History Museum and the Muny
$100 million restoration since the early 2000s has restored prairie and wetland areas

w: Founded in 1984 and relocated through New Windsor, Washington DC and Miami before settling in St Louis in 2011, this nonprofit collects chess history across from the Saint Louis Chess Club. Its collection includes a senet piece, Bobby Fischer's custom chess furniture, and an early chess computer.
s: Bobby Fischer's chess set, and an ancient Egyptian game
_facts: founded 1984, moved through New Windsor, Washington DC and Miami before relocating to St Louis in 2011
located across from the Saint Louis Chess Club, run by the United States Chess Trust
collection includes a senet piece, Bobby Fischer's custom chess furniture, and an early commercial chess computer

w: Missouri's tallest habitable building from 1864 to 1894, this combined federal and state courthouse is where the Dred Scott case originated -- the suit arguing residence in free territory made an enslaved man free, whose rejection helped push the country toward civil war. Now part of Gateway Arch National Park.
s: Where the Dred Scott case began
_facts: combined federal and state courthouse, Missouri's tallest habitable building 1864-1894
site where the Dred Scott case originated
now part of Gateway Arch National Park, operated by the National Park Service

w: Opened in 1997 inside the former International Shoe Company building, City Museum is built almost entirely from repurposed architectural and industrial salvage. The Project for Public Spaces named it a great public space, and USA Today ranked it ninth among 2025's best immersive art experiences.
s: A former shoe factory turned salvage-metal maze
_facts: opened October 1997 in the former International Shoe building
exhibits made largely of repurposed architectural and industrial objects
named a great public space by the Project for Public Spaces
ranked ninth on USA Today's 2025 list of best immersive art experiences

w: Completed in 1960 inside a geodesic half-dome 42 meters across, the Climatron was the world's first fully air-conditioned greenhouse and first geodesic dome enclosed in rigid Plexiglas. It recreates a lowland rainforest with no interior partitions and is named one of the 100 most significant works in US architecture.
s: First air-conditioned greenhouse, built as a dome
_facts: geodesic dome greenhouse completed 1960, 42 meters in diameter
world's first fully air-conditioned greenhouse and first geodesic dome enclosed in rigid Plexiglas
recreates a lowland rainforest without interior partitions
named in 1976 one of the 100 most significant architectural achievements in US history

w: This former Catholic church and its adjoining rectory, now listed on the National Register, once served as the Augustinians' novitiate -- and in 1977 and 1978, one of the novices training there was a young Robert Prevost, decades before he became Pope Leo XIV. A quiet Gate District building with an outsized footnote.
s: Where a future pope did his novitiate, 1977-78
_facts: former Catholic church and rectory in the Gate District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places
site of the Augustinians' novitiate, attended by the future Pope Leo XIV (Robert Prevost) from 1977 to 1978

w: Run by the Missouri Historical Society, founded in 1866, this Forest Park museum covers the state's history and charges no admission -- kept free through a public subsidy from the Metropolitan Zoological Park and Museum District, the same tax base that funds the zoo next door.
s: Free state history museum in Forest Park
_facts: operated by the Missouri Historical Society, founded 1866
located in Forest Park
free admission, subsidized by the Metropolitan Zoological Park and Museum District

w: Japanese architect Tadao Ando designed this concrete gallery on Washington Boulevard for special exhibitions and public programs, with free admission throughout. Known informally as the Pulitzer, it anchors the Grand Center Arts District as one of the city's more architecturally serious art spaces.
s: Tadao Ando's free concrete gallery downtown
_facts: art museum designed by Tadao Ando, located at 3716 Washington Boulevard
known informally as the Pulitzer, in the Grand Center Arts District
free admission

w: Ground broke in 1907 but the New Cathedral wasn't consecrated until 1926. Named for Saint Louis and elevated to basilica status by Pope John Paul II in 1997, it holds one of the largest mosaic installations in the Western Hemisphere along with the archdiocese's burial crypts.
s: One of the West's largest mosaic installations
_facts: ground broken 1907, dedicated with first Mass in 1914, consecrated 1926
designated a basilica by Pope John Paul II in 1997
mother church of the Archdiocese of St Louis, known for one of the largest mosaic installations in the Western Hemisphere, and for its burial crypts

w: Dankmar Adler and Louis Sullivan raised this ten-story terra cotta tower in 1890-91 for brewer and financier Ellis Wainwright, among the very first fully realized skyscrapers. Frank Lloyd Wright called it 'the very first human expression of a tall steel office-building as Architecture.'
s: The building that made Sullivan the skyscraper's father
_facts: designed by Dankmar Adler and Louis Sullivan, built 1890-1891 for Ellis Wainwright
considered one of the first aesthetically fully expressed early skyscrapers
Frank Lloyd Wright called it the first human expression of a tall steel office building as architecture
named one of '10 Buildings That Changed America' by PBS in 2013

w: On May 26, 1780, British-allied Indigenous forces attacked the Franco-Spanish village of St Louis while a simultaneous strike hit Cahokia across the river. Lieutenant governor Fernando de Leyba's garrison of regulars and militia held the fortified town, and the retreating attackers burned crops outside it.
s: The 1780 attack St Louis's garrison held off
_facts: fought May 26, 1780, between British-allied Indigenous forces and Franco-Spanish defenders of St Louis
garrison led by Captain Fernando de Leyba successfully withstood the attack
a simultaneous attack on nearby Cahokia was also repulsed

w: Opened in 1934 as the Municipal Auditorium on the site of Charles Turpin's old Booker T Washington Theater, it was split back-to-back into an arena and an opera house. The Grateful Dead played it seven times, and in 1955 it hosted the Alcoholics Anonymous conference that built AA's service structure.
s: Grateful Dead x7, and where AA built its structure
_facts: opened 1934 as the Municipal Auditorium, renamed Kiel Auditorium in 1943, on the former site of the Booker T Washington Theater
housed a shared arena and opera house, home to the NBA's St Louis Hawks 1955-1968
the Grateful Dead played the venue seven times between 1969 and 1982
hosted the 1955 Alcoholics Anonymous conference that established AA's service structure

w: Henry Shaw, the same 19th-century businessman-botanist behind the neighboring Missouri Botanical Garden, donated this land to the city in 1868. The 289-acre park now stretches 1.6 miles between Kingshighway and Grand, threaded through the Southwest Garden, Shaw, Tower Grove East and Tower Grove South neighborhoods.
s: Henry Shaw's other 289-acre gift to the city
_facts: 289-acre municipal park donated by Henry Shaw in 1868
extends 1.6 miles from Kingshighway Boulevard to Grand Boulevard
part of the same Shaw estate as the neighboring Missouri Botanical Garden

w: Neo-Gothic and second in size only to the Cathedral Basilica, this church earned the nickname Cathedral of South St Louis and holds stained glass by local glazier Emil Frei Sr. Listed on the National Register since 1978, it's run since 2005 by the Institute of Christ the King Sovereign Priest.
s: South St Louis's unofficial cathedral, Latin Mass
_facts: neo-Gothic Catholic oratory, second largest church in the Archdiocese of St Louis
known as the Cathedral of South St Louis, stained glass by Emil Frei Sr

operated since 2005 by the Institute of Christ the King Sovereign Priest, offering the Latin Mass
